QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_28

question.text: The SE Roshni Trust runs an LGBTQIA+ livelihood programme. Under SAS-400, the SIA must approach identification of beneficiaries with special care because:

answer.text: LGBTQIA+ persons are not eligible for SAS-400 support
LGBTQIA+ programmes are not allowed on SSE
LGBTQIA+ identification carries stigma and PII-privacy risk; the SIA must rely on anonymised or pseudonymised data and ensure informed consent in the sampling protocol
LGBTQIA+ indicators are exempt from assurance

explanation.text: The Logic: SAS-400 explicitly covers LGBTQIA+ but the identification process carries stigma and legal/privacy concerns. The SIA must enforce anonymised or pseudonymised beneficiary data, informed consent protocols, and secure data handling — standard GDPR / DPDP-style protections with heightened sensitivity. The Trap: Options A and B are factually wrong. Option D is wrong — all indicators face assurance. Cross-Exam Context: Data-privacy parallels in XXIV (AML — KYC data handling) and DPDP Act references in X-A / X-B (Investment Adviser). Assessor's Pro-Tip: For LGBTQIA+ or gender-minority programmes, design your beneficiary list with a randomised reference ID (not name/Aadhaar). Store the ID-to-name map on a separate encrypted device accessible only to the engagement partner.
